attachments.insertion_landmark: spinous processes C6-T4, spanning about five segments

actions: rotates the trunk to the opposite side

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Linear (or curvilinear in larger patients) probe in parasagittal orientation, 2-3 cm lateral to the spinous process at the target thoracic level (T5 in the original description of the block).
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: The needle passes through trapezius, rhomboid major and the erector spinae muscle group to contact the transverse process; local anesthetic is deposited in the fascial plane between erector spinae (superficial) and this muscle (deep). This muscle lies directly on the lamina/transverse process, in the plane the erector spinae plane (ESP) block targets, rather than being penetrated itself.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Hyperechoic tip of the transverse process contacted by the needle; visible linear anechoic spread lifting the erector spinae muscle mass off the transverse process/this muscle on injection.
structures_at_risk: dorsal and ventral rami of the spinal nerves near the transverse process -- the likely site of action per the original cadaveric/CT dye-spread study
pleura, if the needle is walked laterally off the transverse process (the classic technique avoids this by stopping at bone contact)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: No motor-point/neural-arborization mapping for BoNT injection into this muscle's own belly was found -- consistent with this atlas's established finding that deep paraspinal motor-point data is genuinely sparse compared to limb muscles. What is well documented is the erector spinae plane (ESP) block, whose target plane lies directly superficial to this muscle, deep to the erector spinae group; included here because it is the real, common clinical ultrasound technique relevant to the fascial plane immediately superficial to this muscle, not a claim of a motor point within it.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Forero M, Adhikary SD, Lopez H, Tsui C, Chin KJ (2016) 'The Erector Spinae Plane Block: A Novel Analgesic Technique in Thoracic Neuropathic Pain', Reg Anesth Pain Med 41(5):621-627, doi:10.1097/AAP.0000000000000451 -- original description of the block, including cadaveric/CT dye-spread investigation of its likely site of action
